claims.content: To display file and archive information including size, free space, filesystem type, and progress of executed functions.

goal.raw_text: To display file and archive information including size, free space, filesystem type, and progress of executed functions.

claims.content: User
The PeaZip application is installed and running on the computer system.
The File Manager Interface is active and displaying objects (files, archives, or drives).
The user has access to the 'Browser' menu or equivalent navigation controls within the interface.
The user navigates to a file, archive, or drive location within the File Manager Interface and selects an object or initiates a function that requires displaying its information.

trigger.raw_text: The user navigates to a file, archive, or drive location within the File Manager Interface and selects an object or initiates a function that requires displaying its information.

claims.content: The user views the File Manager Interface which displays a list of objects (drives, files) with columns for Name, Type, Size (B), Free space, and Filesystem.

The system provides a 'Graphic display of currently executed functions' window (PeaLauncher) to show progress information such as Input size, Output size/compression ratio, Time elapsed, and processing speed when an operation is performed.
The interface offers an overview of the objects displayed in the file manager interface to help users handle them better.

The user can toggle between browse mode and flat view mode to display all objects contained in the current path or archive together, using the 'Toggle browse/flat view' option from the Browser menu or by pressing F6.
The user can refresh or update the currently displayed content by selecting 'Refresh' from the Browser menu or by pressing F5.
The user can navigate directly to the computer's root, user's home, desktop, or archive root using keyboard shortcuts (Shift+F2, Ctrl+F2, F2, Ctrl+Shift+F2 respectively) instead of manual browsing.
The user can perform recursive or non-recursive searches within the current folder and subfolders using F3 or Ctrl+F3, which may alter the displayed information set.
The user can access advanced filters to modify the displayed object list by pressing F11.
If the user attempts to use a keyboard shortcut or function that is format-specific and not supported for the current archive type, the system will ignore the command.

If an error occurs during file processing (e.g., during archiving or extraction), the PeaLauncher window may remain open as configured in Settings ('Keep open only if needed (errors, list, test...)') to display the error status instead of closing automatically upon job completion.
The File Manager Interface displays an updated overview of the objects (files, archives, or drives) with their associated information such as Name, Type, Size, Free space, and Filesystem.

If a function was executed during the inspection process, the 'Graphic display of currently executed functions' window (PeaLauncher) shows the final status (e.g., 'Job successfully completed') along with details like Input size, Output size, Time, and processing speed.
The user has gained direct access to other main interfaces of PeaZip (such as archiving or extraction layouts) if navigation options were utilized during the session.
